summary: Feed s123_double to IDS is degraded: 50% of traffic missing VLAN 20 tags and 1.82 Gbps microbursts exceed 1 Gbps IDS port (182% capacity, 9 intervals), causing blind spots and burst drops.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is stripping 802.1Q tags or trunk not forwarding VLAN 20 - required VLAN 20 not seen and 50% of packets are untagged, so IDS has no visibility into VLAN 20 segment.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS is blind to all attacks/lateral movement on VLAN 20; correlation and VLAN-based policies fail, reducing detection coverage by ~50%.

recommended_fix.why: Configure packet broker ingress and egress to preserve 802.1Q tags and explicitly forward VLANs 10 and 20 to the IDS so required segmentation visibility is restored.

findings.root_cause: Microbursts peak at 1.82 Gbps in 1ms intervals vs 1 Gbps IDS port capacity (182% overload across 9 intervals) - single 1G tool port cannot absorb bursts, causing buffer overrun and drops at the broker/tool ingress.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS drops packets during bursts, misses exploits and cannot reassemble flows; needs_full_payload and needs_both_directions inspection fails, creating detection gaps under load.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute traffic across 2+ IDS ports or via load-balancing packet broker function using 5-tuple hashing to keep per-port rate <80% of 1 Gbps and eliminate burst drops while preserving flow coherence.
